Fall to spring co-op switch for accounting major? Would love any advice from accounting upperclassmen/alumni!

**Context:**

* Rising sophomore, accounting concentration, 5 year/3 co-op plan
* Currently on fall co-op cycle, considering switching to spring
* Did freshman year at Oakland so extracurriculars are not that strong (no accounting clubs/orgs, no boston networking yet)
* 3.83 GPA
* Coming back to Boston this fall
* Long term goal is big 4 audit then eventually FP&A

**Why I'm thinking about switching:**

From what I've read, spring cycle lines up with big 4 audit busy season, which is when firms hire more and co-ops actually get substantive work. Fall cycle is during audit shoulder season with fewer slots and less aligned with how big 4 recruits. Recruiting timelines also seem to be better for spring since postings drop in aug/sept of sophomore year.

However, if I switch, I'm in recruiting \~4 months from now with basically zero accounting related extracurriculars from my time at Oakland. BUSN 1103 slots also close soon for fall, so the decision is essentially due in the next week or two before it's too late.

**What I'm trying to figure out:**

* Is spring actually that much better for accounting/big 4 at neu? Would love to hear from anyone who's done either cycle, especially accounting specifically.
* Realistically, what are the odds of landing a big 4 co-op with a thin resume? Are midtier/regional firms the more realistic target? I'd take midtier but just want to know what I'm actually playing for instead of going in delusional.

Would appreciate any advice. Thanks! Spring is nice for a true public accounting busy season from my experience (I just wrapped up an audit co-op). However, you should get in contact with the recruiters at firms you’re interested in regarding their recruiting timelines. Of the Big 4, only Deloitte had openings for this past spring, and of those, only three non-returning students were offered co-ops. Public accounting firms are just recruiting super early now.

As for your question on resume, I would say they scan for GPA and CPA eligibility date first. Then, they look at previous work/extracurricular experience. Networking is 100% the key to getting into those Big 4 pipelines, though. Feel free to DM me if you have any other/more specific questions.

Running out of Claude credits? Mahoraga is here. Northeastern gives us 300 a month, 500 if you're lucky, and premium seats if you're really lucky. By no means is that a small amount; it really is a useful resource that all students should honestly be abusing. (not to cheat on your NUpath courses, but to learn!) 

However tokens are getting more expensive, models are heavier, and i know a bunch of kids that run out before the end of the month. they wait for northeastern, but there are a million students here, and they just can't give us more and more. I personally use claude in my co-op as well, which eats usage. 

"So just use a local model," a smart freshman kid would say. local models run on your own device, and are essentially free. However cloud models like claude, chatgpt, most mainstream subscription models are just smarter and logically sound. 

I built **Mahoraga**, which routes simple tasks using contextual bandits (LinUCB) to local models to cut costs, as well as increase speed. Most work you do consists of bash, edit, etc. honestly pretty quick and light commands that claude really shouldn't have to run. All local inference, all free. Cloud escalation exists but only fires on retry.

So if you're doing CS/Business/honestly whatever nowadays and want to build/ship more often this might be the solution. Clone the repo, fork the repo, everything is **opensource** so you can use claude to implement this if you run into difficulty. Runs on your computer, no one else gets the data except you. (not me, not northeastern). 

Fork, Clone, Star, Steal: [github.com/pockanoodles/Mahoraga](https://github.com/pockanoodles/Mahoraga)

I ran 192 tasks across 8 agents (4 local Ollama models, 4 cloud CLIs) on a 16GB MacBook Pro, forcing round-robin so every agent got every prompt. Quality is scored by a 4-layer heuristic system (novelty ratio, structural checks, embedding similarity, length ratio). Zero API cost for evaluation, and no LLM-as-judge.

Results, tables, and analysis is on the github. If you study CS/DS/AI, you probably know more than me. Input would be appreciated.  Linkedin?
